passages.text: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man,” she said.
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Eve was his wife.
Adam had relations with Eve.
Eve became pregnant.
Eve gave birth to a son.
They named him Cain.
Eve said, “I have brought forth a man with the help of the LORD.”
passages.original: וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־ חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֙הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־ קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.
passages.sermon:
Eve gave birth to another son.  
She named him Abel.  
Abel became Cain’s brother.  
Abel took care of sheep.  
Cain worked the ground.  
Cain grew crops.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣סֶף לָלֶ֔דֶת אֶת־ אָחִ֖יו אֶת־ הָ֑בֶל וַֽיְהִי־ הֶ֙בֶל֙ רֹ֣עֵה צֹ֔אן וְקַ֕יִן הָיָ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ד אֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD, while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
passages.sermon:
Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve.
Abel was Cain’s younger brother.
Cain worked the soil.
Abel kept sheep.
After some time passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD.
Cain’s offering was some of the fruit of the ground.
Abel also brought an offering to the LORD.
Abel’s offering was the best portions from the firstborn of his flock.
The LORD looked with favor on Abel.
The LORD accepted Abel’s offering.
The LORD did not look with favor on Cain.
The LORD did not accept Cain’s offering.
Cain became very angry.
Cain’s face showed his disappointment.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֖י מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃ וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן וַיִּ֣שַׁע יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ הֶ֖בֶל וְאֶל־ מִנְחָתֽוֹ׃ וְאֶל־ קַ֥יִן וְאֶל־ מִנְחָת֖וֹ לֹ֣א שָׁעָ֑ה וַיִּ֤חַר לְקַ֙יִן֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ פָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: “Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Cain.
The LORD asked Cain a question.
The LORD said, “Why are you angry?”
The LORD also said, “Why has your face fallen?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ קָ֑יִן לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Cain.
God said, “If you do what is right, you will be accepted.
If you do not do what is right, sin waits at your door.
Sin wants to control you.
You must rule over sin.”
passages.original: הֲל֤וֹא אִם־ תֵּיטִיב֙ שְׂאֵ֔ת וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תֵיטִ֔יב לַפֶּ֖תַח חַטָּ֣את רֹבֵ֑ץ וְאֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָת֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּמְשָׁל־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
passages.sermon:
Cain was the firstborn son of Adam and Eve.
Abel was Cain’s younger brother.
Cain spoke to Abel.
Cain said, “Let us go out to the field.”
Cain and Abel went out to the field together.
While they were in the field, Cain attacked Abel.
Cain killed his brother Abel.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־ הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יו וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּהְיוֹתָ֣ם בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּ֥קָם קַ֛יִן אֶל־ הֶ֥בֶל אָחִ֖יו וַיַּהַרְגֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: And the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” “I do not know!” he answered. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Cain.
The LORD asked Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?”
Cain replied, “I do not know.”
Cain also said, “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ קַ֔יִן אֵ֖י הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי הֲשֹׁמֵ֥ר אָחִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: “What have you done?” replied the LORD. “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to Cain.\r\nThe LORD asked Cain, “What have you done?”\r\nThe LORD said, “Your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ ק֚וֹל דְּמֵ֣י אָחִ֔יךָ צֹעֲקִ֥ים אֵלַ֖י מִן־ הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Cain.
God said Cain was now cursed.
God said Cain was banished from the ground.
The ground had opened its mouth.
The ground received Abel’s blood.
Cain’s hand shed Abel’s blood.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה אָר֣וּר אָ֑תָּה מִן־ הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּצְתָ֣ה אֶת־ פִּ֔יהָ לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־ דְּמֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Cain.
God said, “When you work the ground, it will not give you crops.
The ground will not help you anymore.
You will live as a fugitive.
You will wander on the earth.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י תַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹֽא־ תֹסֵ֥ף תֵּת־ כֹּחָ֖הּ לָ֑ךְ נָ֥ע וָנָ֖ד תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה בָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
passages.sermon:
Cain spoke to the LORD.
Cain had killed his brother Abel.
God had just cursed Cain.
God said Cain would be a fugitive and a wanderer.
Cain said, “My punishment is too great for me to bear.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל עֲוֺנִ֖י מִנְּשֹֽׂא׃

passages.text: Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
passages.sermon:
Cain spoke to the LORD.
Cain said, “Today You have driven me away from the land.
You have separated me from the ground.
You have hidden Your face from me.
I will be a fugitive on the earth.
I will wander from place to place.
Anyone who finds me will kill me.”
passages.original: הֵן֩ גֵּרַ֨שְׁתָּ אֹתִ֜י הַיּ֗וֹם מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וּמִפָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶסָּתֵ֑ר וְהָיִ֜יתִי נָ֤ע וָנָד֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה כָל־ מֹצְאִ֖י יַֽהַרְגֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Not so!” replied the LORD. “If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.” And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Cain.
The LORD said, “No one will kill you, Cain.”
The LORD said, “If anyone kills Cain, I will punish that person seven times more.”
The LORD put a mark on Cain.
The LORD did this so that no one who found Cain would kill him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כָּל־ הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהוָ֤ה לְקַ֙יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־ אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־ מֹצְאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
passages.sermon: Cain left the presence of the LORD.\r\nCain went to live in the land of Nod.\r\nThe land of Nod is east of Eden.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥צֵא קַ֖יִן מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ נ֖וֹד קִדְמַת־ עֵֽדֶן׃

passages.text: And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
passages.sermon:
Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve.
Cain had a wife.
Cain had relations with his wife.
Cain’s wife became pregnant.
She gave birth to a son.
They named their son Enoch.
Cain built a city.
Cain named the city Enoch.
He named the city after his son.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֙יִן֙ אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־ חֲנ֑וֹךְ וַֽיְהִי֙ בֹּ֣נֶה עִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃

passages.text: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.
passages.sermon:
Enoch had a son named Irad.
Irad had a son named Mehujael.
Mehujael had a son named Methusael.
Methusael had a son named Lamech.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־ עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־ מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּמְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־ מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־ לָֽמֶךְ׃

passages.text: And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
passages.sermon:
Lamech was a man.
Lamech took two wives.
The name of one wife was Adah.
The name of the other wife was Zillah.
passages.original: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ ל֥וֹ לֶ֖מֶךְ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
passages.sermon:
Adah was a woman.
Adah gave birth to a son named Jabal.
Jabal became the ancestor of people who live in tents.
Jabal also became the ancestor of people who raise livestock.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֥לֶד עָדָ֖ה אֶת־ יָבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃

passages.text: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
passages.sermon:
Jubal was Jabal’s brother.
Jubal became the ancestor of all who play musical instruments.
He was the father of those who play the harp.
He was also the father of those who play the flute.
passages.original: וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יוּבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כָּל־ תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃

passages.text: And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
passages.sermon: Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain.\r\nTubal-cain made tools from bronze and iron.\r\nNaamah was Tubal-cain’s sister.
passages.original: וְצִלָּ֣ה גַם־ הִ֗וא יָֽלְדָה֙ אֶת־ תּ֣וּבַל קַ֔יִן לֹטֵ֕שׁ כָּל־ חֹרֵ֥שׁ נְחֹ֖שֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֑ל וַֽאֲח֥וֹת תּֽוּבַל־ קַ֖יִן נַֽעֲמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Lamech said to his wives: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
passages.sermon:
Lamech was a descendant of Cain.
Lamech had two wives.
Their names were Adah and Zillah.
Lamech spoke to his wives.
He said, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice.
Wives of Lamech, listen to my words.
I have killed a man who wounded me.
I have killed a young man who struck me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לֶ֜מֶךְ לְנָשָׁ֗יו עָדָ֤ה וְצִלָּה֙ שְׁמַ֣עַן קוֹלִ֔י נְשֵׁ֣י לֶ֔מֶךְ הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ הָרַ֙גְתִּי֙ לְפִצְעִ֔י וְיֶ֖לֶד לְחַבֻּרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”
passages.sermon:
Lamech spoke to his wives.
Lamech compared himself to Cain.
God promised to avenge Cain seven times if anyone harmed him.
Lamech said he would be avenged seventy-seven times.
Lamech claimed greater vengeance than Cain.
passages.original: כִּ֥י שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקַּם־ קָ֑יִן וְלֶ֖מֶךְ שִׁבְעִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָֽה׃

passages.text: And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam had a wife named Eve.
Adam and Eve had a son named Abel.
Cain, their other son, killed Abel.
Adam again had relations with his wife Eve.
Eve gave birth to another son.
Eve named this son Seth.
Eve said, “God has given me another child in place of Abel.”
Eve said this because Cain killed Abel.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨דַע אָדָ֥ם עוֹד֙ אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁ֑ת כִּ֣י שָֽׁת־ לִ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ זֶ֣רַע אַחֵ֔ר תַּ֣חַת הֶ֔בֶל כִּ֥י הֲרָג֖וֹ קָֽיִן׃

passages.text: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Seth was a son of Adam and Eve.
Seth had a son.
Seth named his son Enosh.
At that time, people began to call on the name of the LORD.
passages.original: וּלְשֵׁ֤ת גַּם־ הוּא֙ יֻלַּד־ בֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱנ֑וֹשׁ אָ֣ז הוּחַ֔ל לִקְרֹ֖א בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃פ
